title: 被问马杜罗被带走：她居然没有强烈谴责，只淡淡说了句方式
speaker: John Lee Anderson

segments.en: At one point you asked, Delsey Rodriguez, do you feel Maduro is unjustly kidnapped?
segments.zh: 你曾问德尔西·罗德里格斯，你觉得马杜罗是被不公正绑架的吗？

segments.en: What does she say to you? And why was that response so illuminating? She said, she paused and then said
segments.zh: 她怎么回答你？为什么那个回应如此说明问题？她停顿了一下然后说

segments.en: in a very kind of tepid way, something along the lines of, yes, the way it was done, you know,
segments.zh: 语气相当平淡，大意是，是的，那种做法，你知道的，

segments.en: that kind of thing. And I said, but I was taken aback because it wasn't a full, you know, it wasn't a pushback. It wasn't condemnatory at all. And I said, well, what about, and there was a hundred
segments.zh: 类似这样的话。我有点意外，因为那不是完全的，不是反驳，完全没有谴责意味。我又问，那关于上百

segments.en: people killed, including European, and she said, yes, some of our people, Cubans too. And she, she withdrew. And it was clear that this was an uncomfortable subject for her. And of course,
segments.zh: 人死亡，包括欧洲人，她说，是的，我们的一些人，还有古巴人。然后她退缩了。显然这个话题让她不舒服。当然，

segments.en: what was fascinating about that moment was that, you know, there are those people plenty in the Nomenclature and the kind of in the know in Venezuela and the U.S. who believe that she was in on
segments.zh: 那一刻引人注目的是，在委内瑞拉和美国的圈内人中，有不少人认为她参与了这个

segments.en: this nudge, that she was given prior knowledge. And that was why she wasn't in Caracas at the time.
segments.zh: 暗示，她事先知情。这就是她当时不在加拉加斯的原因。

segments.en: She has a story that may be true as to why she wasn't there. But on a nearby island, you know, this early New Year's and so on. But I did find that her reaction was odd. So, you know, one,
segments.zh: 她有一个可能属实的说法解释为何不在那里。而是在附近一个岛上，新年刚过等等。但我确实觉得她的反应很奇怪。所以，

segments.en: and the people like Clevverka don't another say, you know, she didn't know beforehand.
segments.zh: 而像克莱弗卡这样的人则说，她事先并不知情。

segments.en: However, we can go back through the public record and we do know that she was in conversations about Maduro, you know, leaving power and her succeeding him with the U.S. And he,
segments.zh: 不过，我们可以回溯公开记录，我们确实知道她参与了关于马杜罗下台并由她接任的对话，与美国方面。而他，

segments.en: Maduro was part of these conversations too. They didn't go anywhere. And then suddenly he was snatched. To be honest, I came away from this whole reporting experience with the feeling that,
segments.zh: 马杜罗也参与了这些对话。但毫无进展。然后他突然就被带走了。说实话，整个报道经历让我感觉，

segments.en: in fact, those prior conversations, which, you know, in which Maduro was supposed to go into Exxon say to Turkey was all a kind of masquerade for a plan that was hatched sometime before to
segments.zh: 事实上，那些先前的对话——你知道，马杜罗本应进入埃克森美孚，对土耳其说的——都像是一场伪装，为了一个早先策划的计划，

segments.en: do what exactly we did, which was snatch him, put him in prison. I'm fascinated by, you know, you said her reaction was kind of odd. I find her position quite odd because she's probably alienated
segments.zh: 具体做什么呢？就是我们做的：把他带走，关进监狱。我很感兴趣，你说她的反应有点奇怪。我觉得她的处境相当奇怪，因为她可能被疏远了。
